highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 introduces an experimental image comparison package for rendering tests.
highlights_body: SkiaSharp.Testing provides configurable acceptance policies and difference images. Ganesh texture-edge sampling and Tizen CPU blur selection also change, and Linux x86 native assets are no longer packaged.

breaking.title: Move Linux x86 deployments to a supported architecture
breaking.body: Linux x86 native assets are no longer built or included in NuGet packages. Move deployments that depend on linux-x86 assets to a supported Linux architecture before upgrading.

bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Testing compares SKImage, SKBitmap and SKPixmap inputs with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets and error metrics, and creates independent caller-owned difference images. The assembly is experimental; opt in by suppressing SKIA4001 with NoWarn or a pragma.

bullets.lead: Keep filtered texture samples inside subset boundaries
bullets.detail: Ganesh sampling now uses an inward offset to avoid including undefined texels outside a texture subset. Texture-edge pixels may differ; CPU and Graphite rendering are unchanged by this sampling option.

Tizen now applies its CPU blur option to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent paths instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur pixels and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance have not been measured locally.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its view projects to the Windows sample solution.
